subject: Sprint 0 Handoff: Streaming, Tool Calls & Structured Output Schema
messages:
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@novushealth.com>

Cc: alex.barnes@novushealth.com
Date: Wed, Jul 7, 2027 at 09:12 AM PDT
Subject: Sprint 0 kickoff + schema questions

Hi Hannah / Camila —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited to start Sprint 0. A few things the engineering team surfaced that we'd like to clarify ahead of the kickoff so we can avoid scope creep:

- Streaming: we expect end-to-end latency below 300ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens). Can you confirm typical steady-state latency targets when streaming to our EU region endpoints?
- Function/tool calling: our EHR connector will send structured update requests and expects deterministic JSON outputs. We want to ensure there is a clear contract for required fields and error shapes.
- Schema: attached is our proposed JSON schema (novus-proposed-schema-v1.json). This is an initial draft — we'll iterate but want Redwood to validate feasibility for streaming + tool-call workflows.

Practical asks before kickoff: a short checklist of what you need from us (API keys, sample payloads, compliance docs) and a proposed agenda for the 60-minute Sprint 0 call.

Alex (cc'd) will join as lead engineer.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Nguyen
Product Lead, Novus Health
Attachments: novus-proposed-schema-v1.json (application/json), novus-data-samples-2027-07.zip (archive)

Subject: Re: Sprint 0 kickoff + schema questions

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick responses inline and a proposed Sprint 0 agenda below.

- Streaming latency: for short prompts we typically target 200-350ms p95 in US regions on our hosted runtime; EU adds ~30-60ms in network delta. We'll run a focused perf-check in your EU region during Sprint 0 and share a latency baseline. If you need stricter p95, we can discuss a dedicated pool.
- Function calls & deterministic JSON: we recommend pinning a schema version and using a tool-calling wrapper so the runtime can surface validation errors as structured responses. We'll provide an example error envelope.
- Schema review: we'll take a pass on novus-proposed-schema-v1.json during the technical prep and flag any fields that may break streaming chunking (very large nested arrays, base64 blobs, etc.).

Sprint 0 (60 min) proposed agenda (we can tighten):
  1) Introductions + success criteria (5m)
  2) Architecture overview + data flow (10m)
  3) Streaming performance expectations + perf-check plan (10m)
  4) Function/tool-call contract & error envelopes (15m)
  5) Schema constraints and acceptance tests (10m)
  6) Next steps, owners, and Sprint 1 scope (10m)

Prep checklist for Novus (what we need before the meeting):
- Sample payloads (sanitized) representative of 99th percentile sizes
- Example error codes you want surfaced by tool-call wrapper
- Contact for infra to coordinate the perf-check whitelist/IPs or VPC peering

I'll set a Calendly for the kickoff; can you share Alex's availability?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Customer Solutions Manager — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sprint 0 kickoff + schema questions

Sarah / team —

Adding a tech-focused checklist and a few constraints we commonly see that affect streaming + tool-calls:

Technical checklist (what we'll validate in Sprint 0):
- Tokenization & max sequence length: confirm tokenizer family or provide a representative sample so we can estimate token counts.
- Batching expectations: whether you expect bursty concurrent requests (we'll size batching and pool config accordingly).
- KV cache & state: if you plan to reuse conversation state between calls, describe TTL and max cache size.
- Error envelope: we prefer a small wrapper with fields {"status","code","message","payload"} so it's easy to route programmatically.
- Schema acceptance tests: provide a small set (~10) of prompts + expected structured outputs we can use as regression tests.

Sample JSON snippet (example only; we'll map to your schema):
{
  "patient_id": "string",
  "observations": [
    {"timestamp": "ISO-8601", "type": "vital", "value": "number"}
  ],
  "update_meta": {"source": "EHR-sync"}
}

Note on streaming + large arrays: if your schema allows unbounded arrays for observations, we may need to truncate or stream arrays in chunks and provide an aggregation step in the tool. We'll flag specific fields after reviewing your v1.

I'll open a shared Drive folder where we can drop the Sprint 0 checklist and test vectors.

- Camila
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Quick operational plan so owners are clear post-kickoff:

Phase 0 (Sprint 0) — technical alignment (owner: Camila)
- Schema feasibility review (Camila)
- Baseline perf-check (Redwood infra team)
- Regression test vector handoff (Novus)

Phase 1 — pilot (owner: Marissa)

- Instrumentation: tracing + token breakdown per route

Phase 2 — rollout (owner: Rafael)
- Increase traffic + set autoscale rules
- Formalize SLOs, fallbacks, and rollback plan
